properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-07, bringing knot theory and its graph-theoretic tools to a question he already opened on 2026-08-18.

KEPT BESIDE `dec:idea-can-a-design-graph-be-reduced-to-its-essential-core` RATHER THAN MERGED INTO IT. It is the same question asked a second time for a different reason, and both reasons matter: the first was four reduction techniques from knowledge-graph practice, this is a formal framework that arrives at one of the same conclusions by an independent route and adds two techniques the first did not name. Merging would lose that the conclusion was reached twice, which is most of its evidential weight.

⭐ THE STRONGEST THING IN THE ANALOGY, AND IT IS AN ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A METAPHOR. A Reidemeister move changes the DIAGRAM, never the knot. Reduction to minimal crossing number does not delete anything from the knot; it finds a better drawing of the same object. Translated: the reduced core is a VIEW OF THE SAME DESIGN, not a smaller design. The earlier node reached "projection, never a write" from reflow2's own doctrine — intent is preserved, findings are asked not repaired, a merge needs a human-asserted DUPLICATES edge. Arriving at the same place from topology, with no knowledge of that doctrine, is the kind of agreement worth more than either argument alone.

⭐⭐ AND IT SUPPLIES THE DECIDABILITY CRITERION THE EARLIER NODE WAS REACHING FOR. That node said what would make this decidable is knowing WHO the core is for. Knot theory says something sharper and checkable: name the INVARIANT. A knot invariant is what must be identical before and after; a reduction that changes it has produced a different knot, and the Jones polynomial exists precisely to catch that. A design-graph reduction with no stated invariant is not reduction, it is deletion with a justification. So the first question is not which algorithm but: what must a reduced view preserve — every requirement's reachability to a verification? every decision's rationale? the set of open questions? Each answer picks a different algorithm, and each is checkable after the fact, which "who is it for" is not.

═══════════ THE TECHNIQUES, TRIAGED ═══════════

TRANSITIVE REDUCTION — already recorded on the earlier node as the only one with no prior art, and already carrying its trap: in a design graph A→B→C and A→C are usually DIFFERENT CLAIMS, so the technique needs a composition table over the typed edge set before it needs an algorithm. Nothing here changes that; the knot framing agrees with it, since a Reidemeister move is valid only for specific configurations rather than for any crossing that looks removable.

k-CORE DECOMPOSITION — NEW, not among the original four, and the one to argue with hardest. It declares the densely-connected nucleus fundamental and peels away weakly-connected leaves as trivia. For a design graph that is close to backwards. Degree measures HOW MUCH SOMEBODY WROTE, not how much a thing matters: a requirement with one edge may be the most important statement in the design and merely under-modelled. This project already knows it under-serves exactly those nodes — `disconnected_community` reports clusters of two or more, so a zero-edge node never surfaces at all, and orphaned requirements are invisible to the heal path for that reason. k-core would systematically discard the population reflow2 already fails to see, and it would look like a clean result while doing it.

BETWEENNESS / BRIDGE NODES — partly built already: `betweenness_centrality` is in use and powers propagation ranking, `pagerank` is imported and unused, and `dec:a-projection-is-named-and-the-battery-runs-over-it` is DECIDED with the first slice named as centrality over the reasoning projection. "Which nodes, if removed, fracture the design" is a genuinely good question and it is one call from being answered on a projection that already has a ruling behind it. This is the cheapest real thing in the whole family.

MINIMUM SPANNING TREE / BACKBONE — NEW, and different from centrality in a way worth keeping apart. Centrality ranks; a spanning tree gives a READING ORDER — the fewest edges that still connect everything. "What would somebody new have to read, and in what sequence" is a different deliverable from "which twenty nodes matter most", and it is closer to what `cap:onboarding` actually needs.

TUTTE AND JONES POLYNOMIALS — recorded because it was raised, and honestly the weakest transfer of the set. The Tutte polynomial counts structures over a graph whose EDGES ARE INTERCHANGEABLE. A design graph's edges are typed and the type carries the meaning: SATISFIES and CONTRADICTS are not two instances of one thing. A polynomial that treats them as such produces a number no one can act on. Left on the record as considered rather than dismissed, because the equivalence it points at — that a structural signature can be invariant under re-drawing — is the useful half, and that half is already captured above as the invariant question.

WHAT IS NOT PROPOSED HERE: building any of it. The earlier node's reading still stands — the useful move is probably ONE view composing what already exists rather than four new features.
properties.name: OPEN — knot theory reframes graph reduction: a Reidemeister move changes the DIAGRAM, not the knot, which argues the reduction is a view; and it asks the question the earlier version could not — what is the INVARIANT?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: the ideas enter as ideas, nothing is promoted, and the objection sits beside each rather than replacing it.

AN AGENT'S READING, offered as a finding rather than an answer. Two of the five items are worth separating from the rest. The invariant question is the real contribution, because it converts an aesthetic goal into a testable one and it applies to every technique in both nodes at once. And the k-core objection is the one place where an off-the-shelf knowledge-graph technique would actively harm this kind of graph, which is worth having written down before somebody reaches for it as the obvious first move.

The reason the knot analogy transfers as well as it does is that both objects have the same shape of problem: a thing whose identity is independent of how it is drawn, and a drawing that accumulates avoidable complexity. Where it stops transferring is that a knot has ONE identity while a design graph is a record of many people's claims over time, some of which genuinely contradict. There is no Reidemeister move for disagreement.
